approach: At constant pressure the work, the change in internal energy, and the heat for a diatomic gas are all proportional to the same temperature rise, through R, Cv and Cp.

steps.text: Write each quantity for a diatomic gas at constant pressure, in units of nRΔT.
steps.equation: dW = nRΔT, dU = n(5/2)RΔT, dQ = n(7/2)RΔT

steps.text: Divide through by nRΔT and clear the fractions by multiplying by 2.

common_mistakes.text: Writing the ratio in the reverse order, dQ : dU : dW instead of the asked dW : dU : dQ, gives 7 : 5 : 2.
Using Cv = 3/2 R, the value for a monatomic gas, in place of 5/2 R for this diatomic gas.
